# Model and source

```{r model-meta, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
ui <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Song_2022_danofloxacin_carp"))
cat("* Citation: ", ui$reference, "\n", sep = "")
cat("* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fvets.2022.868966>\n")
cat("* Open access full text (PMC): <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9019490/>\n")
```

`r ui$description`

Song 2022 is, in the authors' words, the first population PK analysis of
danofloxacin in Yellow River carp. Danofloxacin is a veterinary
fluoroquinolone; the paper's practical conclusion is that a single 10 mg/kg
oral dose gives AUC/MIC and Cmax/MIC ratios above the fluoroquinolone targets
(125 and 10) for pathogens with an MIC of at most 0.016 ug/mL.

# Population

Thirty healthy Yellow River carp (*Cyprinus carpio haematopterus*) were bought
from a commercial farm; 24 were dosed (four tanks of six) and six served as
undosed controls supplying blank plasma (Animals section). Mean body weight was
0.38 kg (range 0.25 to 0.54 kg; per-fish weights are listed in Table 1). Fish
were held at 23.7 +/- 1.2 degC after at least 7 days of acclimation.

Each fish received a single 10 mg/kg body-weight oral gavage of danofloxacin
mesylate (5 mg/mL in saline) and was **sampled sparsely, four times**, from the
tail vein, so that the 24 fish together cover 16 nominal times from 0.25 to
144 h. Plasma danofloxacin was measured by HPLC with fluorescence detection
(LOQ 0.005 ug/mL).

```{r population}
str(ui$population)
```

## Study design (Song 2022 Table 1)

```{r table1}
# Song 2022 Table 1: per-fish body weight, in printed ID order. Four
# four-point schedules cycle across fish 1..24.
schedules <- list(
  A = c(0.25, 4, 16, 72),
  B = c(0.5, 6, 24, 96),
  C = c(1, 8, 36, 120),
  D = c(2, 12, 48, 144)
)
table1 <- tibble::tibble(
  id = 1:24,
  WT = c(
    0.40, 0.37, 0.35, 0.49, 0.31, 0.39, 0.25, 0.41, 0.37, 0.33, 0.37, 0.37,
    0.37, 0.32, 0.37, 0.41, 0.29, 0.53, 0.25, 0.40, 0.42, 0.54, 0.43, 0.37
  ),
  schedule = rep(names(schedules), times = 6)
)
nominal_times <- c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96, 120, 144)
stopifnot(
  nrow(table1) == 24L,
  all(lengths(schedules) == 4L),
  setequal(unlist(schedules, use.names = FALSE), nominal_times),
  # Animals section: mean 0.38 kg, range 0.25-0.54 kg. 0.38 is also the
  # centring weight of Eq. 1.
  min(table1$WT) == 0.25, max(table1$WT) == 0.54,
  round(mean(table1$WT), 2) == 0.38
)
c(n_fish = nrow(table1), n_samples = nrow(table1) * 4L, mean_WT = round(mean(table1$WT), 4))
```

# Source trace

Every value below also carries an in-file comment next to its `ini()` entry in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Song_2022_danofloxacin_carp.R`.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lka` (tvKa) | 2.48 1/h | Table 5, Model 3; SE 0.123, CI 2.24 to 2.73 |
| `lvc` (tvV, V/F) | 47.8 L/kg | Table 5, Model 3; SE 1.90, CI 44.0 to 51.6 |
| `lcl` (tvCL, CL/F) | 0.694 L/h/kg | Table 5, Model 3; SE 0.012, CI 0.669 to 0.718 |
| `e_wt_ka`, `e_wt_vc`, `e_wt_cl` | 0 (placeholders) | Eq. 1 and the text after it: `dKadwt` is "results not shown"; V and CL "by the same algorithm" |
| `(WT / 0.38)^e` power form, 0.38 kg centre | n/a | Eq. 1 and the text after it ("the average body weight of all animals is 0.38 kg") |
| `etalka` variance | 3.45 | Table 5, Model 3, "Interindividual variation omega^2 (CV%)" column |
| `etalvc` variance | 1.19 | Table 5, same column |
| `etalcl` variance | 0.712 | Table 5, same column |
| `propSd` | 0.339 | Table 5, Model 3 residual error; multiplicative error model per the Population Pharmacokinetic Modeling section |
| One compartment, first-order oral absorption, no lag | n/a | Population Pharmacokinetic Modeling ("single compartment extravascular administration") |
| K10 = tvCL/tvV, T1/2 = ln2/K10, AUC0-inf = Dose/tvCL | n/a | Eqs. 2 to 4; results in Table 2 |
| Dose 10 mg/kg BW, single oral gavage | n/a | Drug Administration and Sampling |

Models 1 (no covariates) and 2 (body weight) in Table 5 are intermediate steps;
the packaged model is the final Model 3 that the authors used for every
reported result.

## What the bracketed numbers in Table 5 are

The abstract calls the bracketed omega values (0.203%, 8.40%, 4.35%) the
"coefficient of variation between individuals". They are relative standard
errors. In this paper the "CV%" of an estimate is its SE divided by the estimate,
as the fixed-effect rows show, and a log-normal variance of 3.45 would mean a
between-fish CV of several hundred percent, not 0.2%:

```{r cv-column}
# Song 2022 Table 5, Model 3: (estimate, SE, printed CV%) for the fixed effects
fx <- tibble::tribble(
  ~parameter, ~estimate, ~se, ~cv_printed,
  "tvKa", 2.48, 0.123, 4.94,
  "tvV", 47.8, 1.90, 3.97,
  "tvCL", 0.694, 0.012, 1.77,
  "Residual error", 0.339, 0.014, 4.06
) |>
  mutate(se_over_estimate = 100 * se / estimate)
# The SEs are printed to 2-3 significant figures, so 100*SE/estimate
# matches the printed CV% to within that rounding.
stopifnot(all(abs(fx$se_over_estimate - fx$cv_printed) < 0.2))
# Log-normal CV implied by each omega^2, if the leading number were a CV it
# would not be this.
cv_lognormal <- 100 * sqrt(exp(c(3.45, 1.19, 0.712)) - 1)
stopifnot(all(cv_lognormal > 90))
fx
round(cv_lognormal)
```

So the leading number in the omega column is the variance used in the model,
and the bracketed number is its RSE.

# Reproducing the secondary parameters (Table 2)

Table 2 gives K10 = 0.015 1/h, T1/2 = 47.7 h and AUC0-inf = 14.4 h*ug/mL,
computed from the typical values by Eqs. 2 to 4. Solving the packaged ODE model
at its typical values for a 0.38 kg fish and running PKNCA on the result checks
the ODE structure, the dosing route, the body-weight-normalised units and the
transcribed values against those three numbers.

```{r typical-solve}
mod <- readModelDb("Song_2022_danofloxacin_carp")
mod_typical <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

# Fine early grid for the peak, then out to 720 h (about 15 half-lives) so the
# AUC extrapolation is a small correction.
grid_typical <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.05), seq(24, 720, by = 2))))
ev_typical <- rxode2::et(amt = 10, cmt = "depot") |>
  rxode2::et(grid_typical) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(WT = 0.38)

sim_typical <-
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical, ev_typical, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(id = 1L, treatment = "10 mg/kg")
stopifnot(all(sim_typical$Cc >= 0))
```

```{r typical-profile, echo = FALSE}
sim_typical |>
  filter(time <= 144) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 24, 48, 72, 96, 120, 144)) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma danofloxacin (ug/mL, log scale)",
    title = "Typical-value profile, single 10 mg/kg oral dose",
    caption = "Companion to Figure 1 of Song 2022 (which plots individual observed and predicted data)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# PKNCA validation

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sim_typical |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
nca_conc <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  nca_conc,
  nca_conc |> dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, treatment, time)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_df <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = 10, treatment = "10 mg/kg")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE,
  aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE, lambda.z = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::select(PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
nca_wide[, c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast", "aucinf.obs", "half.life", "lambda.z")]
```

## Gate 1 -- Table 2 secondary parameters

```{r gate-table2}
auc_sim <- nca_wide$aucinf.obs
thalf_sim <- nca_wide$half.life
k10_sim <- nca_wide$lambda.z
pct <- function(sim, ref) (sim - ref) / ref * 100

# Deterministic typical-value solve, so the tolerance only has to absorb
# the 3-significant-figure printing of Table 2 and PKNCA's numerical AUC.
# A 10% error in a transcribed clearance, volume, dose or unit moves these
# by 10% or more.
stopifnot(
  abs(pct(auc_sim, 14.4)) < 1,
  abs(pct(thalf_sim, 47.7)) < 1,
  round(k10_sim, 3) == 0.015
)

tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c("AUC0-inf (h*ug/mL)", "T1/2 (h)", "K10 (1/h)"),
  `Song 2022 Table 2` = c(14.4, 47.7, 0.015),
  Simulated = signif(c(auc_sim, thalf_sim, k10_sim), 4),
  `% diff` = round(pct(c(auc_sim, thalf_sim, k10_sim), c(14.4, 47.7, 0.015)), 2)
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Gate 1: PKNCA on the typical-value solve vs Song 2022 Table 2.")
```

## Comparison against the published NCA

```{r nca-compare}
# Table 2 holds the model-derived AUC0-inf and T1/2, the like-for-like
# reference for a typical-value simulation. The only published Cmax and Tmax
# are from Table 4, a naive-pooled NCA of the sparse data that the authors
# used only to seed initial estimates; they are shown for context and are
# expected to differ.
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~tmax, ~aucinf.obs, ~half.life,
  "10 mg/kg", 0.166, 10.6, 14.4, 47.7
)
simulated <- nca_wide |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "10 mg/kg") |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, cmax, tmax, aucinf.obs, half.life)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = simulated,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", tmax = "h", aucinf.obs = "h*ug/mL", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = paste(
    "Simulated (typical value) vs published values.",
    "AUC0-inf and T1/2 are from Table 2 (model-derived);",
    "Cmax and Tmax are from Table 4 (naive-pooled NCA).",
    "* differs from reference by >20%."
  )
)
attr(cmp, "footnote")
```

The Cmax and Tmax rows are flagged, as expected. The typical-value curve peaks
at about 0.20 ug/mL near 2 h, while the naive-pooled NCA of Table 4 reports a
mean Cmax of 0.166 ug/mL at 10.6 h with SDs (0.321 and 14.5 h) larger than the
means themselves. Table 4's AUC0-inf (4.48) is also a third of the model-derived
14.4. The Discussion calls these NCA values "a lousy prediction ability" and
uses them only as initial estimates, so they are not a validation target.

## Gate 2 -- the PK/PD ratios in the Discussion

The Discussion reports AUC/MIC = 900 and Cmax/MIC = 10.4 at an MIC of
0.016 ug/mL. AUC/MIC is 14.4 / 0.016 = 900, the model-derived AUC; Cmax/MIC is
0.166 / 0.016 = 10.4, the naive-pooled Table 4 Cmax. Recomputing the AUC ratio
from the packaged model checks it against the published conclusion.

```{r gate-pkpd}
mic <- 0.016
auc_mic_model <- auc_sim / mic
stopifnot(
  abs(pct(auc_mic_model, 900)) < 1,
  # The published Cmax/MIC uses Table 4's naive-pooled Cmax, not a model value.
  round(0.166 / mic, 1) == 10.4,
  # The conclusion (both targets met at MIC 0.016) holds with the model Cmax too.
  auc_mic_model >= 125, nca_wide$cmax / mic >= 10
)
c(
  `AUC/MIC (model)` = round(auc_mic_model),
  `Cmax/MIC (model typical value)` = round(nca_wide$cmax / mic, 1),
  `Cmax/MIC (paper, Table 4 Cmax)` = round(0.166 / mic, 1)
)
```

# Between-fish variability

Song 2022 publishes no VPC; Figure 1 overlays individual observed and predicted
concentrations, and the observed data are not tabulated. The cohort below draws
200 fish with body weights resampled from Table 1 and shows the predicted 5th,
50th and 95th percentiles over the 144 h sampling window.

```{r cohort}
# rxSetSeed() fixes rxode2's stream per solver thread but not across thread
# counts, so the assertions below hold for any cohort this model can draw.
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20220406)
set.seed(20220406) # for the base-R weight resampling
n_fish <- 200L
grid_cohort <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.25), seq(26, 144, by = 2))))
wt_draw <- tibble::tibble(id = seq_len(n_fish), WT = sample(table1$WT, n_fish, replace = TRUE))
ev_cohort <- rxode2::et(amt = 10, cmt = "depot") |>
  rxode2::et(grid_cohort) |>
  rxode2::et(id = seq_len(n_fish)) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  left_join(wt_draw, by = "id")

sim_cohort <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_cohort, returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(dplyr::n_distinct(sim_cohort$id) == n_fish)
```

```{r figure-cohort, echo = FALSE}
sim_cohort |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = quantile(Cc, 0.50),
    Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.005, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 24, 48, 72, 96, 120, 144)) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma danofloxacin (ug/mL, log scale)",
    title = "Simulated 5th / 50th / 95th percentiles (individual predictions)",
    caption = paste(
      "Companion to Figure 1 of Song 2022;", n_fish,
      "simulated fish, single 10 mg/kg oral dose. Dashed line: LOQ 0.005 ug/mL."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Gate 3 -- the omega diagonal reproduces as encoded

```{r gate-omega}
per_fish <- sim_cohort |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(ka = first(ka), vc = first(vc), cl = first(cl), .groups = "drop")

realised <- tibble::tibble(
  parameter = c("ka", "vc", "cl"),
  encoded_median = c(2.48, 47.8, 0.694),
  encoded_omega = sqrt(c(3.45, 1.19, 0.712)),
  cohort_median = c(median(per_fish$ka), median(per_fish$vc), median(per_fish$cl)),
  cohort_sd_log = c(sd(log(per_fish$ka)), sd(log(per_fish$vc)), sd(log(per_fish$cl)))
) |>
  mutate(
    median_log_ratio = log(cohort_median / encoded_median),
    sd_diff = cohort_sd_log - encoded_omega
  )

# Cohort statistics: SE(log median) ~= 1.2533 * omega / sqrt(n) = 0.165 at
# worst (ka, omega 1.86), SE(SD) ~= omega / sqrt(2n) = 0.093. The bounds sit
# at about 5 SE and still go red on a variance-vs-SD or decimal-point error,
# which shifts these by 0.5 or more on ka.
stopifnot(
  max(abs(realised$median_log_ratio)) < 0.85,
  max(abs(realised$sd_diff)) < 0.45
)

realised |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Parameter" = parameter,
    "Encoded median" = encoded_median,
    "Encoded omega" = encoded_omega,
    "Cohort median" = cohort_median,
    "Cohort SD(log)" = cohort_sd_log,
    "log(median ratio)" = median_log_ratio,
    "SD difference" = sd_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Gate 3: realised cohort vs the encoded log-normal IIV.")
```

## The body-weight placeholders

With the three exponents held at 0, body weight has no effect: the typical
fish at 0.25 kg and at 0.54 kg (the ends of the observed range) have the same
profile. A user who obtains the authors' estimates can set them with
`ini()`; for example `mod |> rxode2::ini(e_wt_cl = 0.75)` would apply an
exponent of 0.75 on CL/F (an arbitrary illustration, not a value from the
paper).

```{r wt-placeholder}
ev_wt <- rxode2::et(amt = 10, cmt = "depot") |>
  rxode2::et(c(1, 2, 24, 72)) |>
  rxode2::et(id = 1:2) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(WT = ifelse(id == 1, 0.25, 0.54))
sim_wt <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical, ev_wt, returnType = "data.frame")
cc_wt <- tidyr::pivot_wider(sim_wt[, c("id", "time", "Cc")], names_from = id, values_from = Cc)
# Same parameters drawn from the same equations, so this is exact.
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(cc_wt[["1"]], cc_wt[["2"]])))
cc_wt
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **The body-weight exponents are not published.** Eq. 1 retains body weight as
  a power covariate on Ka, V/F and CL/F, centred on 0.38 kg, in the final
  model; the text calls the exponent "results not shown", and no value appears
  anywhere in the paper (there is no supplement). The maintainers kept the
  published covariate structure with the three exponents (`e_wt_ka`, `e_wt_vc`,
  `e_wt_cl`) held at 0 as labelled placeholders. The typical values at 0.38 kg
  are complete and reproduce Table 2 exactly, so predictions for a fish of mean
  weight are as published. For other weights the model returns the mean-weight
  parameters; the observed range is narrow (0.25 to 0.54 kg), so the missing
  exponents move predictions only within about a factor of two in weight. The
  dose and V/F, CL/F are in any case expressed per kg body weight.
* **The omega off-diagonals are not published.** Model 3 adds a "covariance
  model" over the three etas (the Discussion reports a Pearson correlation
  between them and an LRT of 35.9 against Model 2), but no covariance or
  correlation is printed. The etas are independent here. Typical-value results
  (Gates 1 and 2) are unaffected; cohort percentiles will differ from the
  authors' by an amount that depends on the unknown correlations.
* **The bracketed omega numbers are RSEs, not between-fish CVs.** Shown above
  from the paper's own fixed-effect rows; the abstract's wording is not
  followed.
* **Multiplicative residual error = proportional.** Phoenix NLME's
  multiplicative error model is `C * (1 + eps)`, so the reported 0.339 is a
  proportional SD (`propSd`). Table 5's "ug/ml" in the Units column for the
  residual error is not used.
* **Table 1 rows 21 to 24 are partly misaligned in the typeset table.** Their
  weights (0.42, 0.54, 0.43, 0.37) are read in printed order; they reproduce the
  stated mean and range. The sampling schedule is assumed to continue the
  four-fish cycle of rows 1 to 20.
* **Observed data are not reproduced.** No concentration table is published, so
  Figures 1 and 2 cannot be overlaid with observations.
* **Single temperature.** All parameters apply at 23.7 +/- 1.2 degC; the
  Discussion notes that fluoroquinolone elimination in fish depends on water
  temperature.
* **No non-paper-derived parameter values.** Every estimated `ini()` entry is
  transcribed from Song 2022 Table 5; nothing was digitised from a figure,
  obtained by correspondence or carried from an upstream model.
